paper_sections.title: Emotion regulation in social anxiety disorder: behavioral and neural responses to three socio-emotional tasks
Brain responses: BOLD signal temporal dynamics

description.value: The study examined behavioral and BOLD responses during cognitive reappraisal of three socio-emotional stimulus types in adults with generalized social anxiety disorder and healthy controls.

design.value: A between-group fMRI study comparing 27 unmedicated adults with generalized SAD and 27 healthy controls during three socio-emotional tasks, each containing React and Reappraise conditions, with analyses of BOLD signal magnitude and early versus late temporal dynamics.

name.value: Liebowitz Social Anxiety Scale-Self-Report (LSAS-SR)

description.value: This questionnaire assesses both fear and behavioral avoidance of social situations.

name.value: Anxiety Disorders Interview Schedule for DSM-IV-TR Lifetime version (ADIS-IV-L)

description.value: Two PhD-level clinical psychologists assessed each potential participant using the Anxiety Disorders Interview Schedule for DSM-IV-TR Lifetime version.

name.value: Edinburgh Handedness Inventory
Group
Reappraise versus React

source_definition.value: The contrast of Reappraise versus React.

name.value: generalized SAD

description.value: 27 unmedicated (minimum of three months since stopping pharmacotherapy) adults who met DSM-IV-TR criteria for primary generalized SAD.

inclusion_criteria.value: principal diagnosis of current generalized SAD, defined as greater than moderate anxiety/fear for five or more distinct social situations

exclusion_criteria.value: current pharmacotherapy or psychotherapy, history of neurological disorders, and current psychiatric disorders other than SAD, generalized anxiety disorder, agoraphobia without a history of panic attacks, dysthymia, or specific phobia

recruitment_method.value: clinician referrals and advertisements on community and online bulletin boards

diagnostic_instrument.value: Anxiety Disorders Interview Schedule for DSM-IV-TR Lifetime version (ADIS-IV-L)

clinical_characteristics.value: The selected subgroup had LSAS-SR scores ranging from 85–102. Current Axis-I co-morbidity included panic attacks, generalized anxiety disorder, dysthymia, and specific phobia; past Axis-I co-morbidity included major depression, post-traumatic stress disorder, substance abuse, and eating disorder.

medication_status.value: unmedicated (minimum of three months since stopping pharmacotherapy)

education_summary.value: Patients and HC did not differ significantly in years of education.

name.value: healthy controls (HC)

description.value: 27 healthy controls with no lifetime history of psychiatric disorders.

inclusion_criteria.value: no current or past history of DSM-IV disorders

exclusion_criteria.value: HC were not permitted to meet criteria for any current or past psychiatric disorders.

medical_condition.value: no lifetime history of psychiatric disorders

diagnostic_instrument.value: Anxiety Disorders Interview Schedule for DSM-IV-TR Lifetime version (ADIS-IV-L)

clinical_characteristics.value: No current or past history of psychiatric disorders.

education_summary.value: Patients and HC did not differ significantly in years of education.

task_description.value: Participants viewed color photos of faces displaying Ekman facial action coded anger and contempt facial expressions. Each trial included a Look or Reframe cue, a looming harsh facial stimulus, and a negative emotion rating.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed either to react to the faces by engaging in the picture or to reappraise their emotion by thinking of an alternative interpretation.

stimuli.value: Color photos of faces displaying anger and contempt facial expressions, appearing to move closer to the participant to simulate looming.

task_performance_measures.value: Negative emotion rating using a button response pad: “How negative do you feel?” rated from 1 = not at all to 5 = very much.

task_description.value: Participants viewed videotaped actors delivering social criticism or praise. Only the 7.5-second evaluation period of social criticism trials was included in the analysis.

instructions.value: Participants were told either to react to the social criticism by reflecting on how the statement represents something true about themselves, or to reappraise their emotion by thinking that it is not always true or is only a thought, not a fact.

stimuli.value: Videotaped actors delivering social criticism and social praise with harsh or happy evaluation-congruent facial expressions.

task_performance_measures.value: Negative emotion rating using a button response pad.

task_description.value: Participants reacted to or reframed autobiographical social anxiety-related negative self-beliefs embedded in written descriptions of participant-generated social anxiety situations.

instructions.value: Participants were asked either to react to the negative self-beliefs by reflecting on how they represented something true about themselves, or to reframe their reaction by thinking of a positive coping statement that directly challenged the thoughts.

stimuli.value: Written autobiographical situations, 16 sentences describing each situation, and participant-generated negative self-beliefs flashed in uppercase letters.

task_performance_measures.value: Negative emotion rating after each negative self-belief.

modality.value: functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) of blood oxygen-level dependent (BOLD) signal

instrument.value: General Electric 3-T Signa magnet with a custom-built quadrature ‘dome’ elliptical bird cage head-coil (GE Healthcare, Milwaukee, WI, USA)

description.value: Functional volumes were obtained from 22 sequential axial slices. Head movements were minimized using a bite-bar and foam padding.

description.value: Preprocessing included analysis of potential outliers, volume registration to a base image, motion correction, 4 mm isotropic Gaussian spatial smoothing, high-pass filtering, linear detrending, conversion into BOLD signal percentage change, and exclusion of the first four images of each functional run.

steps.value: volume registration to a base image
conversion into BOLD signal percentage change in each voxel
the first four images of each functional run were excluded, to allow for T2* equilibration effects
For the Criticism and Belief tasks, the two functional runs were concatenated prior to statistical analysis.

hrf_model.value: Cohen’s gamma variate model of the hemodynamic response function

model_settings.value: Baseline parameters removed mean, linear, and quadratic trends, and motion-related variance in the BOLD signal. Regressors for the React and Reappraise conditions were convolved with the hemodynamic response function. BOLD signal intensity was computed as percentage of signal change.

Individual brain maps were converted to Talairach atlas space and second-level group statistical parametric maps were produced. Multiple comparisons were corrected using AlphaSim, with voxel-wise P <0.005 and cluster volume >244 mm3 to protect against false-positive cluster detection at P <0.01.

name.value: React

description.value: Participants were instructed to react normally without any attempt to control, modify, or regulate any reactions.

name.value: Reappraise

description.value: Participants were instructed to try and down regulate negative emotion reactions by actively reinterpreting the meaning of the emotion inducing stimulus.
